42716.why: A whole temple wall of the Medicine Buddha, fifty feet wide, surrounded by attendants. Walk up close and it holds still for you.

39328.why: Shiva dances inside a ring of fire, one foot raised, perfectly balanced in the middle of everything ending and starting again.

39557.why: Kuncan painted dense wooded mountains at dusk with a poem about hiding out from the world. A picture for going inside.

40020.why: Hongren, a monk-painter, drew a valley with almost nothing in it. The title says you can hear spring arriving.

49132.why: Gong Xian built these wintry mountains out of thousands of small dark dots. Bleak, patient, and strangely comforting.

48932.why: Ma Shouzhen painted one orchid and one rock in a few quick strokes. Nothing wasted, nothing missing.

45420.why: Kano Tanyu's landscape in moonlight is mostly mist and silver. A screen for a quiet evening.

829385.why: Kano Motonobu filled a pair of screens with birds, blossom and running water. Spring, at full volume.

64872.why: Genki painted a year in Kyoto, with hundreds of small people out walking in every season. You are one of them.

39666.why: A blue-and-white jar with a dragon wrapped all the way around it, mid-flight and grinning.

42124.why: A Tang dynasty woman on horseback, sitting easy, ready to ride out. Thirteen hundred years old and still going somewhere.

38448.why: Avalokiteshvara, the bodhisattva of compassion, carved by the Tenth Karmapa with a soft, almost shy face.

640049.why: Lake Biwa in four seasons, painted by a calligrapher. The same water, four different moods.

36108.why: A huge votive painting of a lion tumbling through peonies, made to hang in a shrine and be seen from far away.

42059.why: A jade boulder carved into a Daoist paradise: pines, pavilions and tiny immortals climbing toward the top.
